translation: The Blessed Lord said: This physical body, O son of Kunti, is technically designated by the title of the Field (Kshetra). And he who directly observes and monitors this machinery is called the Knower of the Field (Kshetra-jna) by the ancient seers of reality.
simple_explanation: This verse establishes the foundational distinction of Vedic psychology. Your physical body, your passing thoughts, and your emotional anxieties are things that can be observed by you. Because they can be observed, they represent objects of experience—they belong to the Field. You are the conscious Subject doing the observing. Confusing the Field with the Observer is the root of all human bondage.

translation: Understand Me, O descendant of Bharata, to be the ultimate Knower of the Field operating within all individual fields across the universe! A thorough, systematic comprehension of the boundary between the Field and its Knower constitutes genuine, authentic wisdom—such is My definitive view.

What that Field is, what its primary properties are, how its modifications unfold, from what sources it projects, who that Observer is, and what his innate powers are—listen now to My succinct, summary explanation.

This science has been celebrated by ancient rishis in multiple ways, across diverse Vedic hymns, and articulated with razor-sharp logical definitions in the definitive verses of the Brahma Sutras (hetumadbhir-vinishchitaih).

The five gross cosmic elements, individualized egoism, the discriminating intellect, unmanifest primordial nature, the ten sensory and motor organs, the single processing mind, and the five objective realms of sensory perception;
simple_explanation: Verses 5 and 6 present a complete catalogue of the variables that form the material world. Notice that psychological phenomena like desire, hatred, pleasure, and pain are explicitly classified as parts of the Field. They are objects that arise within the material nervous system; they are not essential attributes of the pure spiritual Soul.

translation: Desire, hatred, pleasure, pain, the biological physical framework (sanghatah), the manifest biological life-current (chetana), and emotional fortitude (dhriti)—this summarizes the complete layout of the Field along with its structural modifications.

Absolute humility, freedom from vanity and ostentation, non-violence, patient endurance, straight integrity, dedicated service to wise mentors (acharya-upasanam), internal and external cleanliness, unswerving stability, and mastery over the lower self;

Systematic detachment toward sense objects, absolute freedom from egotism, and a realistic, constant intellectual awareness of the systemic vulnerabilities and distress inherent in birth, death, old age, and disease;

Freedom from clinging possessiveness, absence of obsessive identification with children, spouse, or property, and maintaining an unswerving, balanced equanimity of mind under both pleasant and unpleasant turns of fortune;

Unswerving, single-minded devotion focused continuously upon My presence through Yoga, a natural preference for quiet, undisturbed locations (vivikta-desha-sevitvam), and a healthy distaste for empty, shallow socializing;

Constantly anchoring the life around the knowledge of the inner Self (Adhyatma-jnana), and maintaining an unswerving focus upon the ultimate purpose of realization—this complete catalogue of intellectual attributes is declared to be genuine wisdom (Jnanam); anything which deviates from this baseline is nothing but raw ignorance (Ajnanam).

I shall now clearly define that ultimate Objective which must be known, mastering which a human being tastes the nectar of immortality. It is the beginningless, supreme Brahman, which cannot be defined either as manifest existence (Sat) or as unmanifest non-existence (Asat) in a material sense.
Operating everywhere through the hands, feet, eyes, heads, mouths, and ears of all living creatures across the world, that Divine Presence wraps around and pervades everything that exists.

It illuminates the operations of all sensory faculties, yet It is completely devoid of physical sense organs. It remains entirely detached, yet It is the absolute Sustainer of all existence; It is free from the modes of material nature (nirgunam), yet It is the ultimate Enjoyer and Evaluator of those modes.

It resides both outside and inside all living creatures; It is both the unmoving and the moving variables of nature. Owing to its transcendent subtlety (sukshmatvat), It is inconceivable to the raw logical mind; It is extraordinarily distant, yet It is intimately near, seated right inside your heart.

It remains completely undivided, yet It appears dynamically split among distinct individual entities across creation. That ultimate Reality must be recognized as the absolute Sustainer of all creatures (bhuta-bhartru), the power that swallows them down during dissolution, and the source that projects them forth during creation.

It is the absolute Light behind all lights, declared to be far beyond the darkness of material ignorance. It is wisdom itself (Jnanam), the object to be known, the goal of all realization, permanently seated within the heart of everyone.

Thus has the structure of the Field, the nature of wisdom, and the ultimate Object to be known been succinctly explained. My devotee, absorbing this science, becomes fully qualified to attain My divine nature.

Know that both material nature (Prakriti) and the conscious Spirit (Purusha) are completely without beginning. And understand clearly that all physical modifications and the operational modes of nature (Gunas) project directly from material nature alone.

Material nature is declared to be the sole operating cause behind the mechanical production of physical effects, biological instruments, and agency (karya-karana-kartritve). While the conscious Spirit is said to be the experiencing cause behind the internal perception of pleasure and pain (bhoktritve).

For when the conscious Spirit embeds and identifies itself with material nature (prakriti-stho), it develops a craving for the modes born of nature. This psychological attachment to these qualities acts as the sole operating cause driving it into noble or degrading physical wombs across multiple lifetimes.

The supreme conscious Spirit residing within this physical body is also designated by the titles of the immediate Witness (upadrashta), the Permitter (anumanta), the Sustainer, the ultimate Experiencer, the Great Sovereign, and the higher Self (Paramatma).

He who systematically understands the conscious Spirit and material nature along with its operational modes in this manner—no matter what external roles or duties he may be actively executing in the material world, he is never subjected to rebirth.

Some perceive the higher Self within their own consciousness through deep meditation (Dhyana); others arrive at this realization through the analytical philosophy of knowledge (Sankhya-yogena); while others capture it through the path of selfless action (Karma- yogena).

Still others, who lack the depth to practice these direct methods, listen to instructions from wise masters and begin their worship based on faith. Relying sincerely upon authoritative teaching (shruti-parayanah), they also successfully cross beyond the territory of death.

Whichever entity comes into visibility in this world, O foremost of the Bharata dynasty— whether it belongs to the unmoving or the moving variables of creation—know that it exists exclusively due to the structural combination of the Field and its conscious Knower.

He who perceives the supreme Lord as residing equally across all living creatures, as the imperishable Witness within all passing, perishable forms—he alone possesses genuine, accurate vision (sah pashyati).

For, recognizing the identical Divine Presence as residing equally everywhere across creation, he refuses to degrade or self-sabotage his higher path through lower mental whims. Guided by this balanced sight, he ascends straight to the highest Destination.

He who clearly perceives that all physical actions are executed in every possible way exclusively by the mechanical properties of material nature, and tracks the higher Self as remaining the non-attached Non-Doer (akartaram)—he possesses genuine vision.

When a practitioner directly perceives that the entire diverse variety of all living creatures is anchored within a single underlying Unity, and tracks how all diversity radiates from that source—he then achieves absolute realization of Brahman.

Owing to its beginningless nature and its complete freedom from material attributes (nirgunatvat), this immutable, higher Self, O son of Kunti, does not perform any binding actions and is never contaminated, even though it resides within the physical body.

Just as the all-pervading space (akasham), owing to its infinite subtlety, is never stained or dirtied by the passing smoke or dust suspended within it, similarly, the pure conscious Spirit, though residing everywhere inside the physical body, is never contaminated by bodily changes.

Just as a single sun hanging in the sky illuminates this entire world with its light, similarly, the conscious Master of the Field (Kshetri) completely illuminates the entire Field with the light of awareness, O descendant of Bharata!

Those who perceive through the sharp eye of wisdom (jnana-chakshusha) this precise distinction between the Field and its conscious Knower, and grasp the scientific method of liberating the conscious spirit from its enslavement to material nature—they ascend straight to the Supreme.
